report.headline: Usage rate projected to fall from 25.0% to 19.2% in the move to the NBA, while the true shooting projection carries no predictive value.

projection.text: Projected usage rate in the NBA is 19.2%, down from a 25.0% usage rate in the G League source season, landing just below the league-average 20.1% usage rate (sd 5.2%) for the target season.

risks.text: The true shooting projection of 53.6% should not be trusted: the model's 4.7% error is no better than simply guessing the league average, so this figure carries no predictive value.

Even the more reliable usage projection has an 80% interval of 14.0% to 24.5%, a range covering roughly two standard deviations of the NBA's usage distribution (sd 5.2%), leaving substantial uncertainty about the player's actual role.
The projection rests on only 45 historical G League to NBA transitions, and the source season itself covered just 43 games and 1,451 minutes.
A relatively high turnover rate of 11.9% and a heavy reliance on three-point attempts (33.9% of shots) in the G League add further variance to how the player's efficiency will translate.

strengths.text: In the source season the subject posted a 26.1% assist rate alongside 5.779 assists per 75 possessions, well above a modest 11.9% turnover rate.
Scoring output was strong at 20.886 points per 75 possessions on a 57.4% true shooting percentage, +0.32 standard deviations above the G League average that season.
Usage sat at 25.0%, +1.10 standard deviations above the G League average, indicating a featured offensive role before the move.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage rate runs from 14.0% to 24.5%, a span of roughly two standard deviations of the target league's usage distribution (sd 5.2%), and the 95% interval widens further to 11.2%-27.3%; the model can rank this player relative to peers but cannot pin down an exact usage rate. The true shooting projection has an out-of-fold error of 4.7%, identical to the trivial league-mean baseline's 4.7%, so it should be treated as carrying no information beyond the league average.
